belief: 孔明灯是诸葛亮为了传递军情发明的
truth: 「孔明灯」这个名字不能证明发明者是诸葛亮；这项归属仍是传说，最初发明者尚不明确。
detail:
教育部《重编国语辞典修订本》介绍孔明灯时，特地保留了「传说」二字。台湾文献馆也并列两种解释：一种说诸葛亮发明了它来传递军情，另一种说灯的外形像孔明画像中的帽子。两种说法都是起源传说，不能互相当作证据。

能够具体核对的材料，要和这些传说分开看。台湾文献馆引述杨廷理 1803 年在伊犁所作《洋灯》的小序，描述了竹篾为骨、外糊白纸、点燃后升空的灯。这能说明当时已有这类装置，却不能把发明时间定在 1803 年，更不能据此追认三国时代的发明者。

同一篇文章还引述连横对童年孔明灯的回忆，其中与诸葛亮行军的联系只是听来的说法。现有这些材料足以说明名字和传说怎样联系在一起，却不足以给最初发明者定名。
origin: 台湾文献馆指出，来历模糊的发明常被附会到历史名人身上。「孔明灯」这个名称又让后来的记述很容易顺着名字解释来历；久而久之，介绍中的「相传」便容易被读成确定的发明记录。
instead: 可以说：「孔明灯也叫天灯，传说与诸葛亮有关，但发明者尚无可靠定论。」讲民俗故事时保留「相传」，介绍技术史时再问出处能追到哪一步。

sources.label: 教育部《重编国语辞典修订本》——「孔明灯」释义明确标为传说
国史馆台湾文献馆 ——《平溪天灯》：发明说与帽形命名说

en.belief: Zhuge Liang invented Kongming lanterns to send military messages
en.truth: The name ‘Kongming lantern’ does not establish Zhuge Liang as the inventor. That attribution remains a legend, and the original inventor is uncertain.
en.detail:
Taiwan’s Ministry of Education dictionary explicitly calls the attribution a legend. Taiwan Historica gives two traditional explanations: Zhuge Liang invented the lantern for military communication, or its shape resembled the hat in his portraits. Neither story verifies the other.

Dated descriptions tell us something more limited. Taiwan Historica reproduces the preface to Yang Tingli’s poem ‘Foreign Lanterns,’ written in Yili in 1803. It describes a paper-covered bamboo frame that rises when lit. This documents such a device at that time; it does not establish 1803 as its invention date or identify an inventor in the Three Kingdoms era.

The article also quotes Lian Heng’s childhood recollection of Kongming lanterns. His link to Zhuge Liang’s military campaigns is explicitly something he had heard. These accounts show the name and the attribution circulating together, but do not settle who first invented the device.
en.origin: Taiwan Historica notes that inventions with unclear origins are often attached to famous historical figures. The name ‘Kongming lantern’ invites later writers to explain the object through Zhuge Liang. In retelling, the qualifier ‘according to legend’ can easily disappear.
en.instead: Say: ‘Sky lanterns are also called Kongming lanterns. Tradition links them to Zhuge Liang, but their inventor is not securely established.’ Keep the qualifier when telling the story, and distinguish it from a documented invention history.

sources.label: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Revised Mandarin Chinese Dictionary — Kongming lantern, explicitly described as a legend
Taiwan Historica — Pingxi Sky Lanterns: invention and hat-shape traditions
Taiwan Historica — Sky Lanterns in Historical Records: Yang Tingli and Lian Heng

belief: 风筝是墨子发明的，后来又由鲁班改进
truth: 古书记下了墨子和公输子制作木鸟的故事，却不足以确定风筝的唯一发明者或完整的技术传承。
detail:
《韩非子·外储说左上》讲墨子花三年做成木鸢，飞了一天就坏了；《墨子·鲁问》讲公输子用竹木做鹊，书中说它飞了三天不落地。两段都接着讨论技艺是否实用，人物和细节也不同。它们没有交代一条「墨子发明、鲁班接手改进」的完整技术传承。

而且，古人自己就质疑过其中的夸张。王充在《论衡·儒增》中讨论鲁般、墨子的木鸟故事，认为「三日不集」的飞行时长被说过了头。所以，不能只取故事中的神奇部分，再当成经过核实的飞行纪录。

这些文字讲的是木鸢、竹木鹊，没有交代牵线方式和借风飞行的结构。把它们与后来的风筝联系起来，可以作为起源讨论；单靠这些段落，还不能确认木鸟究竟是什么装置，更不能确定谁独自发明了今天所说的风筝。
origin: 「墨子先造木鸟，鲁班再用竹子改进」的完整故事，今天仍见于旅游文化介绍；北京旅游网的英文介绍就这样叙述，并以传说开头。转述时如果省去这个限定，古代木鸟故事便容易变成一份确定的发明履历。
instead: 可以说：「中国早期典籍记有墨子、公输子制作木鸟的故事，常被联系到风筝起源；具体装置和最初发明者仍难确定。」保留这些有趣的记载，也保留它们没有回答的问题。

en.belief: Mozi invented the kite, and Lu Ban later improved it
en.truth: Ancient texts tell wooden-bird stories about Mozi and Gongshu Zi, but they do not establish a sole inventor of the kite or a complete chain of development.
en.detail:
The Han Feizi tells of Mozi taking three years to make a wooden bird that broke after one day of flight. The Mozi describes Gongshu Zi making a magpie from bamboo and wood, supposedly staying aloft for three days. Both passages turn to whether craftsmanship is useful. Their characters and details differ, and neither sets out a complete ‘Mozi invented it, then Lu Ban improved it’ sequence.

Ancient readers also questioned the embellishment. In the Lunheng, Wang Chong discusses the wooden-bird stories about Lu Ban and Mozi and treats the three-day flight claim as an exaggeration. The spectacular detail should not be presented as a verified flight record.

These passages describe wooden birds without explaining tethering or a wind-driven design. They are relevant to discussions of kite origins, but cannot by themselves establish exactly what devices were involved, still less who single-handedly invented the kite as we understand it today.
en.origin: The neat sequence of Mozi making a wooden bird and Lu Ban improving it with bamboo still appears in cultural tourism writing. Visit Beijing recounts it explicitly as a legend. Drop that qualifier in retelling, and an ancient story begins to sound like an established invention history.
en.instead: Say: ‘Early Chinese texts describe wooden birds made by Mozi and Gongshu Zi, often linked to kite origins. The devices and the original inventor remain uncertain.’ Keep the interesting accounts, along with the questions they leave unanswered.

belief: 街亭失守后，诸葛亮靠城楼弹琴的空城计吓退了司马懿
truth: 弹琴退敌是《三国演义》的经典情节；类似故事早在裴松之注中就有，而裴松之紧接着提出了反驳。
detail:
《三国演义》第九十五回把这场戏写得很具体：街亭失守后，诸葛亮在西城只剩二千五百军，打开城门，在城楼焚香弹琴；司马懿怀疑有伏兵，领军退走。熟悉的画面可以在小说里找到，不能直接当成战事的实录。

不过，这个故事也不是到了《演义》才突然出现。《三国志·诸葛亮传》的裴松之注保存了一则郭冲所述的旧事：地点是阳平，诸葛亮留万人守城，司马懿率二十万军来；诸葛亮开城门、偃旗息鼓，使对方疑有埋伏。这里已经有空城疑兵的骨架，细节却和小说不同。

更重要的是，裴松之在引文后立即驳斥：诸葛亮初屯阳平时，司马懿还镇守宛城，直到曹真死后才与诸葛亮在关中交战；兵力调度等叙述也有疑点。史书注释保存一种说法，可能正是为了辨析它。漏掉后面的反驳，就会把「有这段故事」误读成「史家确认此事发生」。
origin: 从早期轶事到小说，人物对峙被写得越来越具体；京剧《失街亭·空城计·斩马谡》也保留了城门大开、诸葛亮抚琴、司马懿退兵的场面。小说和舞台让这幅画面很熟悉，但传播广并不会补上它的史料缺口。
instead: 介绍时加上「《三国演义》里的」最稳妥。谈历史则说明：更早有类似传说，裴松之还明确质疑过。这里辨析的是诸葛亮弹琴退司马懿这一场景，不是否认历史上可能出现过示弱疑兵的战术。

en.belief: After losing Jieting, Zhuge Liang played a zither on the city wall and frightened Sima Yi into retreat
en.truth: The zither-playing scene is a classic episode in Romance of the Three Kingdoms. A similar earlier story appears in Pei Songzhi’s annotations, immediately followed by his objections.
en.detail:
Chapter 95 of Romance of the Three Kingdoms gives the familiar scene: after Jieting is lost, Zhuge Liang has only 2,500 troops at Xicheng. He opens the gates and plays a zither on the tower. Suspecting an ambush, Sima Yi withdraws. This is a passage in a novel, not a battle report.

Yet the story predates the novel. Pei Songzhi’s annotations to Zhuge Liang’s biography in the Records of the Three Kingdoms preserve an account attributed to Guo Chong. It places Zhuge Liang at Yangping with 10,000 men against Sima Yi’s 200,000. Open gates and concealed military activity make Sima Yi suspect a trap. The outline is similar, but the details differ.

Pei then challenges the account: when Zhuge Liang first stayed at Yangping, Sima Yi was stationed at Wancheng; they confronted one another in Guanzhong only after Cao Zhen’s death. He also questions the troop deployments. A historian can preserve a story to criticize it. Omitting those objections turns evidence that a story circulated into apparent proof that it happened.
en.origin: The anecdote becomes a vivid confrontation in the novel. The Beijing opera sequence ‘Losing Jieting, the Empty Fort Strategy, and Executing Ma Su’ likewise presents open gates, a composed Zhuge Liang playing his instrument, and Sima Yi’s retreat. Its literary and theatrical familiarity does not resolve the historical problems.
en.instead: Introduce it as ‘the scene in Romance of the Three Kingdoms.’ For history, explain that an earlier account exists and Pei explicitly challenged it. This entry concerns Zhuge Liang’s zither-playing encounter with Sima Yi, not whether commanders ever used apparent weakness to suggest a trap.

sources.label: Romance of the Three Kingdoms, chapter 95 — the fictional zither-playing episode
